timestamp.unit: seconds since 2023-01-01T00:00:00 (Chicago local time as published; not UTC)

edgeIndex.note: index into chicago-roads edges (one representative direction of the street; use edgeReverse for the other); 4294967295 = no edge within 60 m

edgeOffset.note: distance along the edge from its source node (fraction of snapped polyline x edgeLength)

snapDistance.note: distance from crash point to edge, rounded, capped at 255

properties.description: City of Chicago traffic crashes in 2023 (CPD-reported, crash_date in 2023) with position, time, severity, and a precomputed snap to chicago-roads (edgeIndex + edgeOffset) for network K-function / linear referencing.
properties.licence: City of Chicago Data Portal Terms of Use (open public data)
storyNotes: 109,711 crashes with coordinates in 2023 (1043 dropped for missing/invalid location); 23,280 people injured, 150 killed in 142 fatal crashes.

98.9% snap within 60 m of a drivable edge (median snap 11.0 m); the rest have no drivable edge nearby (e.g. lots, alleys, edges outside the strongly connected component) and carry edgeIndex 4294967295.
Busiest edge: 151 crashes on one block of LAKE SHORE DR SB. Rush hour: 15:00 is the peak hour; busiest weekday Friday.
Most common primary cause after 'unable to determine'/'not applicable': Failing To Yield Right-Of-Way (12,360).

Severity mix: 85% no injury; 2,018 incapacitating or fatal. Streets with most crashes: Western Ave (2,936), Pulaski Rd (2,924), Cicero Ave (2,601), Ashland Ave (2,359), Halsted St (2,093). Crashes are confined to the street graph, so a planar K-function over-states clustering that a network K corrects.
